title: API signature drift detection
description: The most mechanical drift: the code's public signatures change but the spec (docs, IDL, OpenAPI) doesn't. Detectors diff extracted signatures against the spec on every commit and flag additions, removals, and type changes — the spec is either updated or the code reverted, decided explicitly.
method: Extract signatures from code and spec; diff; classify (additive/breaking); require spec updates or explicit waivers per change.
usage: Run in CI on every change to public surface; treat unacknowledged drift as a build failure.

demo.code:
documented, actual = {'f(a:int)'}, {'f(a:int)', 'g(b:str)'}
print('drift: new function g() undocumented -> spec update required')

title: Test-oracle staleness detection
description: Tests encode the spec; when tests are updated to match new behavior without a spec change, the oracle has drifted. Detectors flag test changes that alter expectations (not just coverage) and require the spec rationale — 'the test changed because the requirement changed' must be stated, not assumed.
method: Diff test expectations across commits; flag expectation changes; require linked requirement/spec updates for each.
usage: Review expectation-changing test edits carefully; they're spec changes in disguise.

demo.code:
print('test_t7: expected 200 -> 404 (expectation changed)')
print('no linked spec change -> BLOCKED: state the requirement or revert')

title: Model-behavior drift (ML)
description: Deployed ML models drift from their validated behavior as data shifts: accuracy decays, calibration worsens, feature distributions move. Drift detectors track prediction distributions, feature drift (PSI/KS tests), and ground-truth accuracy where labels exist — retraining is triggered by measurement, not schedule.
method: Monitor feature distributions and prediction stats; compare to training baseline; retrain on significant drift; validate before swap.
usage: Establish baselines at deploy; monitor continuously; retrain on drift, not on calendar.

demo.code:
print('feature age: PSI 0.31 vs baseline (>0.25 = significant)')
print('DRIFT -> retrain triggered, challenger validated, swapped')

title: Configuration drift detection
description: Running config drifts from declared config: someone tweaks a flag in production 'temporarily' and forgets. Detectors continuously compare actual vs declared configuration and alert on divergence — GitOps' closed loop, where the declared state is the spec and reality must match it.
method: Declare config in version control; continuously reconcile actual vs declared; alert and optionally auto-remediate divergence.
usage: Declare everything; reconcile continuously; treat manual production tweaks as incidents.

demo.code:
print('declared: replicas=3; actual: replicas=5 (manual tweak)')
print('DRIFT detected -> alerted, reconciled to 3')

title: Dependency behavior drift
description: Upgraded dependencies can drift behaviorally while keeping signatures: same function, subtly different results. Detectors run the application's golden tests against dependency upgrades and diff behaviors — the upgrade's behavioral delta is reviewed like a code change.
method: Golden test suite; run against old and new dependency; diff behaviors; review the delta as part of the upgrade PR.
usage: Maintain golden tests for dependency-sensitive behaviors; review every behavioral delta.

demo.code:
print('lib v2.3->v2.4: 2 golden outputs differ (rounding change)')
print('delta reviewed: acceptable -> upgrade approved with note')

title: Spec coverage tracking
description: Drift also means the spec no longer covers the code: new features with no spec, tested behaviors nobody specified. Coverage tracking maps code to spec clauses and reports unspec'd territory — the spec's blind spots, prioritized by risk, scheduled for specification.
method: Map code regions to spec clauses; report unmapped regions; prioritize by risk; schedule spec writing.
usage: Require spec coverage for new features; work down the unspec'd backlog by risk.

demo.code:
print('spec coverage: 78% of code mapped to clauses')
print('unspec\'d: payments/refund.py (HIGH risk) -> spec sprint scheduled')

title: Schema evolution compatibility
description: Data schemas (protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema) drift across services: a producer adds a field, a consumer's old schema rejects it. Compatibility checkers (backward/forward/full) verify each schema change against the compatibility policy before it deploys — drift that breaks consumers is caught at the registry, not in production.
method: Register schemas; check each change against the compatibility mode; reject breaking changes; version explicitly.
usage: Enforce compatibility at the registry; version schemas; test consumers against new schemas pre-deploy.

demo.code:
print('schema v7: removed field "name" (BACKWARD mode)')
print('REJECTED: breaks v6 consumers -> use optional field instead')

title: Documentation-code consistency checks
description: Docs drift fastest: examples that no longer run, parameters renamed in code but not docs, architecture diagrams of a system that no longer exists. Consistency checkers extract claims from docs (signatures, examples, diagrams-as-code) and verify each against the code, failing the docs build on mismatch.
method: Extract doc claims; verify against code (signatures, runnable examples, generated diagrams); fail docs build on mismatch.
usage: Generate what can be generated; verify the rest; never let docs build green while wrong.

demo.code:
print('docs claim: f(a, b); code: f(a, b, c=1)')
print('MISMATCH -> docs build FAILED until synced')
